I'm 54 this year, been farming these 24 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My old man taught me, and I mostly finished primary school. My wife and I are at home — our kids work in the city and send a bit back now and then, but not much. I have to watch every yuan. I split my land into two pieces: 16 mu I do wheat then maize back-to-back every year, and the other 8 mu I grow cotton. I copied the cotton from my neighbor Lao Wang — he's been doing it for years and it pays better than maize when the price is right.

The wheat went in last October like always. I plowed the field and put down base fertilizer then — about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, same as I always do. Now it's April and the wheat is at jointing. I can see it needs a boost, so I'll topdress with about 25 jin of urea per mu. Last year I tried a little less and the wheat turned yellow, so I went back to my usual amount. I'll irrigate three times this spring: now at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling if it's dry. The well water costs electricity money so I don't waste it, but wheat needs water. I'll spray herbicide once — the weeds are already coming up. For harvest in June, I'll hire the combine machine like everyone else. I expect about 400 jin per mu if the weather holds.

For cotton, I'm planting it right now on the 8 mu. I bought new hybrid seed this year — about 2 jin per mu. I plowed and harrowed the field in March. I'll put down base fertilizer at planting: about 30 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Cotton needs a lot of attention. I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is very dry — too much water and it grows leaves instead of bolls. I'll spray insecticide for aphids and herbicide once. At flowering I'll topdress with another 15 jin of urea per mu. My wife and I will do the thinning and spraying, but come September and October we'll hire women from the village to help pick. Cotton is a lot of hand work. I hope for about 250 jin of lint per mu, but you never know with the weather.

For maize, I won't plant until mid-June, right after the wheat comes off. There's barely a week between — sometimes only five days. I hire a tractor with rotavator to till right behind the combine, then I plant by machine. I buy hybrid maize seed — costs more but the yield is worth it. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 jin per mu, and then topdress with urea at the big leaf stage. Maize in summer usually gets some rain, so I only irrigate once or twice. I'll spray herbicide once. The maize should be ready by late September. I expect around 450 jin per mu.

Money is always tight. I keep some cash back for doctor visits or emergencies — I've seen neighbors go broke because they spent everything on fertilizer and then a family member got sick. So I don't push for maximum fertilizer. I do what worked last year, maybe a tiny bit more if I have spare cash after buying seeds, but never less. Total input costs this year will run me about 12,500 yuan. My wife helps with all of it, but with just us two we have to hire machine operators and cotton pickers. That's life.
